description: Headless GIMP: append (or, with filter_id, re-edit in place) a NON-DESTRUCTIVE adjustment filter — stays live and re-editable; nothing bakes into pixels until gimp_export, and gimp_filter op=delete removes it again. `type` picks the adjustment: curves, levels, exposure, brightness_contrast, hue_saturation, color_balance, color_temperature, shadows_highlights, saturation, vibrance, sharpen, noise_reduction, gaussian_blur, clarity. A field another type uses is refused, naming this type's own fields. A filter applies to ONE layer (`layer_id` or `layer`, else the selected or top layer), not to the flattened image — on a multi-layer document, say which layer. For type vibrance, the knob is the `vibrance` field — `saturation` on that type is a separate plain multiplier that normally stays untouched. curves: ONE filter per channel — add separate filters for red and blue rather than one filter for both; points are [input, output] 0-255 pairs including the endpoints. hue_saturation and color_balance likewise carry ONE `range` per filter. gaussian_blur: radius in pixels at full resolution; combine with a saved-selection mask for soft-focus or background-blur effects. clarity: midtone local contrast (the `clarity` field, 0..100); reach for it instead of a large-radius sharpen. A re-edit (filter_id) MERGES: any field you omit keeps the filter's existing value, so re-editing {contrast: 50} on a brightness_contrast filter doesn't reset brightness. Only filters Editmamei created can be re-edited; one added in the GIMP GUI is refused (delete and re-create it). `mask` (a saved selection channel name) confines a NEW filter — fixed at creation, cannot change on a re-edit. ORDER MATTERS: straighten / flip / resize the canvas first, then crop, THEN add any masked adjustment — rotate, flip, and resize all refuse outright once a masked adjustment filter exists, or any filter not created by Editmamei (for example one added in the GIMP GUI). color_temperature's direction is counter-intuitive: raising to_kelvin WARMS the image. Check the stack afterward with gimp_filter (op=list).

amount.description: sharpen only. GEGL's unsharp-mask strength MULTIPLIER, not a percent: 0.5 is the default, 1.0 is strong, and values above ~3 are extreme. Default (when creating): 0.5.

black_level.description: exposure only. Shadow black-point shift. Default (when creating): 0.0.

channel.description: curves/levels only. 'value' adjusts all channels together (tone); red/green/blue adjusts ONE channel (color) — a filter carries only one channel, so shifting color needs separate filters for red and blue. Default (when creating): value. Omitted on a re-edit keeps the existing filter's own channel.

clarity.description: clarity only. Midtone local contrast (a high-pass blended in Overlay): 25 is subtle, 50 clear, 100 strong. Shadows and highlights barely move, so it does not clip or darken the photo the way a large-radius sharpen does; use this instead of one. Above about 60 a light halo can show where a dark edge meets a bright sky. It only adds contrast: to soften texture, use gimp_add_effect type=surface_blur. Default (when creating): 25.

compress.description: shadows_highlights only. How far the shadows/highlights effect reaches toward the midtones: higher confines it to the darkest and brightest tones. Default (when creating): 50.

filter_id.description: Re-edit this existing filter IN PLACE instead of adding a new one (must match `type`'s operation). Any per-type field you omit keeps the value it already had — this is a MERGE, not a reset. The values gimp_filter op=list reports for it are in these same field names and units, so they can be passed straight back. The mask is fixed at creation and cannot change on a re-edit. Only filters Editmamei created can be re-edited (gimp_filter op=list shows source: "editmamei"); re-editing any other filter (for example one added in the GIMP GUI) is refused, because its current values cannot be read back exactly — delete it and re-create it instead. A re-edit keeps the filter on its own layer; `layer` and `layer_id` are ignored.

from_kelvin.description: color_temperature only. The temperature the photo currently looks shot under. Default (when creating): 6500.

gamma.description: levels only. Midtone gamma, 0.1..10 — >1 brightens midtones, <1 darkens. Default (when creating): 1.0.

highlights_ccorrect.description: shadows_highlights only. Colour saturation kept in the recovered highlights (0 = none, 100 = full). Default (when creating): 50.

image.description: Image id, as returned by gimp_open_document.

in_high.description: levels only. Input white point; must stay above in_low. Default (when creating): 255.

in_low.description: levels only. Input black point; must stay below in_high (an empty or inverted input range is refused). Default (when creating): 0.

layer.description: Layer name. Defaults to the selected layer, or the topmost layer if none is selected. The filter applies to that ONE layer, not to the flattened image, so on a multi-layer document name the layer you mean. A layer inside a layer group can be named directly.

layer_id.description: Layer id, as gimp_inspect (and any tool that creates a layer) reports it. Takes priority over `layer`, and is the only way to address one of two layers that share a name.

mask.description: Name of a saved selection channel, confining a NEW filter to it. Only valid when creating (no filter_id) — a filter's mask is fixed at creation. ORDER MATTERS: straighten / flip / resize the canvas first (gimp_transform_canvas, gimp_resize_image), then crop, THEN add masked adjustments — rotate, flip, and resize all refuse outright once any masked adjustment filter exists on the image, or any filter not created by Editmamei (for example one added in the GIMP GUI), since they cannot keep a mask aligned through those transforms. Cropping afterward is always safe.

name.description: Label for a new filter, e.g. "Lift shadows". Made unique automatically.

out_high.description: levels only. Output white. Default (when creating): 255.

out_low.description: levels only. Output black. Default (when creating): 0.

points.description: curves only. [input, output] pairs, 0-255 each, ascending input — include the endpoints, e.g. [[0,0],[64,90],[255,255]] lifts shadows. Required when creating (no filter_id); omitted on a re-edit keeps the existing curve.

radius.description: shadows_highlights: spatial falloff radius, 0.1..1500 (default 100 when creating). sharpen: unsharp-mask std-dev, 0..1500 (default 3.0 when creating). gaussian_blur: blur radius (std-dev) in pixels at full resolution, 0..1500 (default 1.5 when creating). clarity: high-pass radius, the size of the detail it works on, in pixels at full resolution, 1..500 (default 40 when creating); about 1% of the long edge suits most photos, 40 for 12 MP, 60 for 24 MP. All four are SPATIAL (radius-scaled on the proxy preview, see gimp_overview).

range.description: hue_saturation: one of all/red/yellow/green/cyan/blue/magenta (default 'all'). color_balance: one of shadows/midtones/highlights (default 'midtones'). ONE range per filter: adjusting reds and blues, or shadows and highlights, takes one filter per range (the same rule as one curves filter per channel). Passing a value from the other type's set is rejected by the bridge naming the real allowed set for the `type` you gave.

saturation.description: hue_saturation: -100..100 percent (default 0 when creating), the field that actually adjusts saturation for that type. vibrance: a SEPARATE, plain saturation multiplier layered on top of the vibrance field below — 1.0 = unchanged (default when creating), 0..10 scale. It is NOT the vibrance knob; normally leave it alone and use `vibrance` instead. The bridge enforces the precise range for whichever `type` you gave.

shadows_ccorrect.description: shadows_highlights only. Colour saturation kept in the lifted shadows (0 = none, 100 = full). Default (when creating): 100.

strength.description: noise_reduction only. Neighbourhood size. Default (when creating): 4.

to_kelvin.description: color_temperature only. The corrected target temperature. COUNTER-INTUITIVE DIRECTION: RAISING to_kelvin WARMS the image (it means "render as if shot under this light" — a higher assumed light temperature reads as a warmer correction). Example: from_kelvin 6500, to_kelvin 8000 renders WARMER, not cooler. Default (when creating): 6500.

type.description: Which adjustment to apply/re-edit. Each type maps to exactly one GEGL/GIMP operation; see the per-field descriptions below for which fields apply to which type.

vibrance.description: vibrance only. THE vibrance control — a vibrance adjustment must set this field, not `saturation` (a separate, plain multiplier for this type that normally stays at its default). The scale follows Photoshop's Vibrance: +10 to +30 is a natural boost, +50 a strong one; negative values desaturate. Unlike Photoshop's, it lifts already-saturated colors (a blue sky, a bright shirt) about as much as muted ones, so check those areas with a histogram above about +50. Default (when creating): 0.

whitepoint.description: shadows_highlights only. Shifts the white point: positive brightens the top end, negative pulls it down. Default (when creating): 0.

name: gimp_add_adjustment
